method.control: Implementation is limited to one dependency-free in-memory Timestamp value/error module, focused tests, and morize-core re-exports. No clock acquisition, calendar/timezone conversion, arithmetic, formatting/parsing, serialization, persistence, transport mapping, or third-party dependency is authorized.
method.review_separation: An independent semantic reviewer must review the exact implementation head for normalized Unix-part semantics, negative-time ordering, bounds validation, absence of clock/calendar/wire behavior, scope containment, and required evidence separately from the implementing agent before acceptance.
method.rollback: Revert the timestamp primitive implementation commits; no persisted format, migration, clock state, or user data depends on this Grain.

outcome: morize-core exposes one dependency-free Timestamp value with a unique normalized in-memory instant representation as signed Unix seconds plus a nanosecond fraction, deterministic ordering/value semantics, and strict nanosecond bounds, without adding clocks, timezone/calendar behavior, parsing/formatting, serialization, persistence, transport semantics, or third-party dependencies.
rationale: P1 explicitly requires timestamps, and docs/DATA_MODEL.md requires the first data-model SpecGrains to refine timestamp representation. This Grain defines only a normalized in-memory instant value using signed Unix seconds plus a non-negative nanosecond fraction so ordering is deterministic across pre/post-epoch values while clock acquisition, calendar/timezone conversion, serialization, persistence, and domain timestamps remain separate decisions.
title: Add normalized timestamp primitive
